core_territory: The Atlantic coastal sugar belt - Pernambuco and the Bahian Reconcavo above all
domain_territory: The Northeastern coastal strip from Rio Grande do Norte to Sergipe; Rio de Janeiro's coast
sphere_territory: Espirito Santo; the southern Bahian cocoa coast; overlaps the Caribbean plantation sphere by sea
anchor_cities: Salvador; Recife; Olinda; Maceio; Rio de Janeiro
founding_population: Enslaved Africans and their descendants, brought for the sugar engenho
characteristic_institution: The sugar engenho (plantation mill), financed partly with Dutch capital
notes: Portugal moved 1,187,000 Africans against 523,000 Europeans across 1500-1760 - a ratio of 2.27 to 1, hitting 4.5 to 1 in 1640-1700. Brazil went from 94.1% Indigenous in 1570 to 55.6% Black by 1825. COASTAL STRIP ONLY - the Nordeste's interior is a different Brasil entirely.

core_territory: The Amazonian main stem and its river network
domain_territory: The whole Norte region - AC, AP, AM, PA, RO, RR, TO
sphere_territory: Western Maranhao; parts of Mato Grosso; the Cerrado fringe
anchor_cities: Manaus; Belem; Santarem; Porto Velho; Rio Branco
founding_population: Indigenous-European mixing on a river-based settlement logic
characteristic_institution: An extractive economy - rubber and forest products - with rivers rather than roads as the organizing infrastructure
ibge_regions_it_crosses: Norte; reaches into Nordeste via Maranhao
notes: Roughly matches the IBGE Norte, which is 45.27% of Brazil's land area but only 4.7% of its people - an emptiness that is historical rather than natural.

core_territory: The semi-arid Northeastern interior - the sertao
domain_territory: Northern Minas Gerais; parts of Goias and Tocantins
sphere_territory: The caatinga fringe; the transition toward the Cerrado
anchor_cities: Petrolina; Juazeiro; Feira de Santana; Campina Grande; Montes Claros
founding_population: Neither plantation nor Indigenous but a third thing made by the backlands - a cattle population adapted to drought
characteristic_institution: Open-range cattle on semi-arid land, with a distinct religious and musical culture
notes: THE HEADLINE MISMATCH. IBGE treats the Nordeste as one region of 54.6 million. Ribeiro splits it along the rain line into coastal Crioulo and interior Sertanejo - two societies with different founding institutions, populations, religions in practice and politics. Any division keeping the Nordeste whole is choosing an administrative boundary over an institutional one.

core_territory: The Sao Paulo interior and southern Minas Gerais
sphere_territory: Mato Grosso do Sul; the Triangulo Mineiro
anchor_cities: Sao Paulo; Campinas; Ribeirao Preto; Uberlandia; Londrina
founding_population: Tupi-Portuguese mixing and the bandeirante expeditions - largely mameluco men who spoke the Lingua Geral Paulista rather than Portuguese
characteristic_institution: Subsistence farming before coffee arrived; before that, the bandeiras - slaving expeditions into the interior
ibge_regions_it_crosses: Cuts across Sudeste / Sul; ignores the Sao Paulo state line completely
notes: A NEAR-EXACT PARALLEL TO WOODARD'S GREATER APPALACHIA: unplanned, mixed, mobile, violent, beyond the reach of any colonial government - and they determined the country's borders, pushing Portuguese control hundreds of miles past the 1494 Tordesillas line, formalized by the Treaties of Madrid (1750) and San Ildefonso (1777). Corresponds to no administrative unit at all, which is the clearest demonstration that Ribeiro's map is the Woodard-type map.

core_territory: The far south - Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina and Parana
domain_territory: The gaucho campanha of southern Rio Grande do Sul; the German and Italian colony belt of the Serra Gaucha and Santa Catarina valleys
sphere_territory: Parts of Sao Paulo; the Uruguayan and Argentine border zone
anchor_cities: Porto Alegre; Curitiba; Florianopolis; Caxias do Sul; Blumenau; Pelotas
founding_population: Azorean, German, Italian and Polish immigrant colonies plus the gaucho pastoral tradition of the campanha
characteristic_institution: Two different institutions inside one region: smallholder immigrant colony agriculture, and extensive pastoralism on the campanha
notes: Roughly matches the IBGE Sul, but the gaucho campanha and the immigrant colony belt are two different things inside it and could be split. Highest HDI in Brazil. A development trajectory unlike the rest of the country.
